To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) E-beam irradiated solar sail and thermal blanket materials have comparable or better tensile strength and tensile modulus properties than non-irradiation controls.
E-beam doses up to 12 kGys do not compromise the mechanical properties of solar sail and thermal blankets materials.
E-beam doses of up to 12 kGry can be used to sterilize aerospace materials without compromising their mechanical properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of a non-thermal sterilization method for heat sensitive aerospace materials.
the development of a new sterilization technology for heat sensitive materials that can be used in planetary missions.
the evaluation of the mechanical properties of aerospace materials (thermal blankets, solar sail and epoxy adhesivEccobond™) to Ebeam sterilization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the tensile strength and the tensile elongation at break of the solar sail film and the tensile strength of the thermal blanket “mesh” and the tensile and shear strength of the epoxy adhesive, Eccbond-9™ were not affected by the E-beam sterilizations.
the mechanical properties of the materials tested were not significantly compromised by E-beam sterilizing doses of 12 kGys, which are sufficient for microbial sterilization.
E-beam sterilized solar sail and thermal blanket materials are suitable for planetary missions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
E-beam sterilized materials are not significantly compromised and can be used in space missions.
E-beam doses up to 20 kGy can be used on aerospace materials without significant changes to the mechanical properties.
E-beam sterilized materials can meet the stringent PP requirements for planetary missions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
E-beam sterilized materials can be successfully used for planetary missions.
E-beam sterilized aerospace materials can meet NASA’s PP specifications.
12 kGyr E-beam dose is a viable option for PP applications of aerospace materials such as solar sail and thermal blankets.
